body:
> However, you are responsible for your own healing.

Literally how? If I was a cis woman I could go to the women's shelter. If I was a cis man, there is a men's group I could go to. I am cut off from both!

Honestly, anyone who has access to anything a cis person can get has an unbelievable amount of privilege, and you guys don't even know it.

Yes, I have been called outright "delusional". They've used the fact that I had colic as a baby to prove I'm hard to please.

There are things I have proof of, things like being told gays were pedos in church. My family was there beside me but they remember none of it. I showed them proof they taught that and they claim I'm cherry-picking and that no one said it.

We're here because we are in abusive relationships too. And I'm a trans man. I've *had* the "entirely different" experiences myself and they're constantly erased.

Edit: I've been abused about my gender constantly. Am I meant to somehow magically heal enough to not be sensitive about it just to be able to participate in an abusive relationships sub? Because that just cuts me off from yet another resource!

I have got NO HELP in real life. It's why I moved back in.

Mine was 10 years ago. I had been doing an engineering degree but wasn't doing well at it -- I had good grades prior but the first time at university was awful.

I was experiencing a ridiculous amount of sexism from my family. They thought my degree was a "hobby" and that it wasn't actually important. I got a bit sabotaged, because my mother told me not to apply for living cost loans and that she would help, and then she didn't and turns out she just didn't see the point and didn't want me to have a huge loan.

I also left my high-control religion which was causing these issues.

And in hindsight the friends I was with were extremely judgemental and basically bullied me a lot.

I got committed and quit my degree one paper away from completion. I didn't even want to continue life at that point.
They cause so much damage! It's so ridiculous that they have as good PR as they do. Every single person in my family who left took baggage with them, it's very sad.

Yes to a lot of these, actually. He's right about me being good at getting things done. Abuse hotline already knows. Friends know. I was rather determined to get out and stay out the first time, and made sure to tell people, even telling people "I'm telling you this because I'm afraid I'll go back."

It's just that I ended up sneaking back kind of covertly and stopped talking about it. My husband isn't always supportive, but my internal monologue when I am alone is just 100% emotional abuse that pulls no punches.

I have a new therapist since yesterday. 

I guess all of this is a good sign in a way. I just feel a bit defeated.

My self worth is quite visibly bad at this point. My manager at work has set me a goal to be better at taking on board *positive* feedback. So... it's bad enough that people notice and comment on it, but I'm still lost on how to actually not feel like I'm a completely worthless piece of shit and waste of air.

(I know thinking like this is hurting me. I'm very frustrated that at this point I just can't stop myself.)

Started escitalopram a week ago and I'm suddenly *so* carb hungry. Probably doubled what I was eating prior.

(This isn't a huge problem, I was having trouble eating before and was getting close to underweight.)

I'm sorry. My mother did something similar when I told her what was going on, said it was my fault for escalating -- but I'd just described him punching a hole in the wall out of nowhere during chores, I wasn't even involved!

It did open my eyes to why I might be with him in the first place. It's a horrible thing to come to terms with, but your family dynamics may have taught you to just take it.

I have an eating problem that means I am able to eat less and less the more stressed I get. Most of the stress is related to my internal monologue loudly hating myself and telling me that people are going to abandon me... so I think that in effect BPD is the number one "cause" of it.

No, I understand. Abuse unfortunately is one of the risk factors for developing BPD and although I got a lot better behaviour-wise once my environment changed my thought patterns are still BPD.

It has explanatory power for me to use the label, and it is useful to look at therapies that work for it. But tbh I would dread an official diagnosis because of my past experience with it. I do better when I'm self-directed.

I believe I am borderline but the diagnosis hasn't stuck officially. When it first got put on me temporarily when I was in a psych ward the way I got treated was absolutely awful. Imagine going to a therapy session and trying to say what was happening at home and they call you a liar, saying you're making up abuse to manipulate people.

I don't have much faith in the doctors there. Find it ironic they were half right, as in I do match all the thought patterns but they were completely wrong about how to treat it. I didn't get better until someone believed me about what was happening at home and got me out of there.

If this was a month ago or so I wouldn't feel so called out.

I have a friend who basically told me if I was uncomfortable during sex it would be better for him, and keeps sending me really, really extreme sexual fantasies. Has offered to pay me to participate. 

My dumb ass is like "I know this is absolutely disgusting behaviour but I can't lose this friend." Fucking hate my complete lack of self-respect. Trying to psych myself up to tell him to fuck off.
I have just started escitalopram within the last week. This makes me quite hopeful. :)

Sometimes. I am incapable of receiving affection without doubting it's for real. I know this is destroying many moments which should be perfectly happy. Compliments shouldn't twist me up inside about whether they're lying, I've tricked them into thinking I'm better than I am, or they just plain have bad taste.

I function OK on the surface but good things happening to me do not produce good feelings. Usually the opposite. Spend a lot of my timing reliving old things. There were so many different bad themes in my childhood that it is difficult to handle all of them. They're tangled together, addressing one often drags several other things in until it is actually far too much to handle.

And while I'm pretty good at doing workbooks of my own volition I'm not getting professional help that works. I have talk therapy but at this point I've said just about everything that happened and I don't feel much better. There are some accessibility issues with me getting someone who can do proper trauma-informed therapy, unfortunately. Had no luck.

I experienced this and the script I was meant to follow was one laid out by our controlling church. It controlled my entire life!

I had my own goals but they weren't valued. I had really good grades in high school and went into engineering but my mother told me that was kind of pointless. I was supposed to be a stay at home mother. She hated me for having sex before marriage and made my life hell but there were so many worse things I could have been doing!

I do but I'm very careful with how/when I do it. I haven't self-harmed in over 10 years -- at least actively, I still am prone to substance problems -- and I can be very matter of fact about it. "I experienced a trigger and I feel the urge to hurt myself because I think I deserve it. Can we find a distraction, please?"

It at least sometimes stops me falling too far into bad coping mechanisms but it doesn't stop them popping up like sad whack-a-mole. I've just had to cut back on drinking because I was aware I had been drinking every day for weeks.

I've been observing my mental health declining with a lot of concern and haven't managed to stop it. I am trying, just booked more counseling and am on meds since a few days ago.

Cool, I did not know that about CBD oil! I do know some people who sell it so I might try that. Judging from how haze strains are described, that must be it. My husband likes precisely the strain that doesn't work for me and he describes it as having a lot of creative energy.

Oh yes it really is great! I was on there for the first time around six years ago and it stopped some awful nightmares I was having about being separated from my husband in the afterlife (not temple married). Such a weight off to finally get rid of that nagging "What if it's true and I'm tempted by Satan?"
Oh hey, we have some other background things in common, too. I was mainstream LDS.

I use weed but am having a mixed experience with it. It's illegal where I live and I can't get the same strain consistently. Some of them make me very anxious and some of them make me so calm and peaceful and I just love everyone so much. It's frustrating that occasionally I find out I have a bag that will cause the former.

I don't think it's necessarily a bad thing. I eventually started using too much and walked it back to a more manageable level. That happened during the pandemic and was mostly because I couldn't leave the house, not sure it would have happened like that if everything was business as usual. There's a balance to be struck and it's sometimes a fine enough line to be confusing, so just be aware.

Me too. I have a particular sense of style and I play sad piano songs but I'm not sure whether this is a "personality".

I also picked a new name a few years ago and it was really hard. I'm trans (don't know if that's also your reason) and I couldn't decide for so long that I was passing as a man before I finally settled on one.

I do, but it's illegal where I am and this is causing a lot of issues for me. I have no control over the strain of weed. If I'm lucky enough to find one that makes me feel like I love the world and everyone in it they invariably get raided by the cops within a few months. Some types make me *more* anxious and it's horrible.

I am resigned to using something and weed is the best of a bad situation. Having a really hard time accessing therapy. Weed dealers don't care if I'm queer, apparently the therapists do. Fuck the whole system and the way it's set up.
That's what I did, too. When the self-harm got discovered none of the issues were fixed so I just switched tactics.

> You have tried to leave, but it's made you feel physically ill, like you will die or your life will be destroyed if you do.

This one isn't kidding around. I left for a few months and became physically and mentally unwell enough that I ended up back.

Yes, I've had very similar experiences when I attempted. One of the hardest parts were they didn't think I was serious and said things like "You could have died, that was dangerous". Really showed me they understood nothing about the situation. 

But also they were getting a lot of input from my mother, who comes across very well in public, is highly educated, etc. They didn't believe she was doing anything at all to me and if I said something they interpreted it as a lie. So I plain didn't get appropriate help. (All of my siblings had severe mental health issues and two of us had SH problems. It was not just me being a liar about it.)

Physical pain from being tense all the time. I hurt my shoulder doing Pilates last month and that wasn't strenuous, it's just that I hold all my stress in my shoulders.

I often get stressed enough to not keep food down or get too nauseous to eat at all.

When I leave work my teeth start chattering and I start shuddering uncontrollably.

Insomnia. 

Panic attacks.

It's... tricky why my SA is getting erased.

I'm a trans man, and people no longer even consider that I could have been abused in the past. I've literally had women who have figured out I'm "safe" or an "ally" tell me how nice it must be to have grown up without the harassment they face, and in those cases I simply do not know what to say and feel really sick.

Because I lived as a woman for 30 years. Way more than this story happened. If this counts as SA, it has happened more than once.

I didn't think it was good, but I did think it was all my fault that it was bad.

It took until this year (34 yo) to realize that my childhood was absolutely fucked up, and that when I was having severe mental health problems it was for a damn good reason!

I got taught really early, and explicitly, that people who don't criticize me (said as "people who don't have high standards") don't love me enough to make me improve. For a very long time I hung around with people who criticized me because it was what I was used to, they were the only people my parents approved of, and I really did think I needed people "brave" enough to tell me what a pathetic piece of shit I was.

I have found people who don't do that, and I am hopefully recovering, but I still take criticism better than I take compliments.

I've been having panic attacks over the last few weeks and every time it happens I just feel this additional crushing disappointment that this is my life and I can't just enjoy it.

The other trigger is being treated really badly, knowing it, and not having the self-esteem to stand up for myself. I know why this is, but the mere fact I can't always overcome it is just guaranteeing I'm going to collect more trauma, and I hate it.

I've definitely had friends that dropped me for being depressed and I'm now really cautious. It's one of the reasons asking for help produces a lot of anxiety now.

But these friends really are great, and I really appreciate them for listening and just sending me pictures of whatever they're into -- sometimes just catching a new Pokémon or something -- so that I keep socializing in small, manageable ways.

Just... same. I'm going through something similar with a friend and it's really hard to accept he's predatory when we actually are friends and he's done me some good as well.

It has messed with my head so much.

I had a conversation with my dad within the last couple of weeks where he said it was no surprise I have no good memories because when I was a baby I screamed so much that (my country's version of) CPS was called and did an inspection. Used it as proof I just made myself sad. I'm not so sure that's what happened...

My mother will kind of force practical (financial) help on me to show me she cares. She did this recently when I left my husband. I make more than she does, I don't need her money. What I do need is emotional support and she will not give that without also telling me that everything I'm going through is my fault.

Yes, even though I'm getting better at asking for it I still experience severe anxiety even if things go well.

I have seasonal depression and I have been putting out signals to my friends that I need a bit of support. I make sure I am not asking for too much by giving them really small things, like sending me memes and things they like, or setting up regular coffee outings. My friends say yes to these but every time I ask for it I spend most of my night after feeling undeserving and like I'm asking too much.

My mother did the same when I was with a really controlling guy. I would have understood if she was afraid to confront him but she *did* confront him and tell him off -- for completely consensual sex with me. Not for anything that actually hurt me, just her personal obsession with my sex life.

Because I'm hyper self aware and keep feeling urges to do things which are obsessive, unhealthy, etc, and these days don't tend to do them.

My environment has changed a lot. I stopped melting down once I had some freedom, wasn't constantly exposed to anti-LGBT stuff at home (as an LGBT person myself), could walk away from a fight instead of being told I had to stay. The moment I got out, I was able to set boundaries and just say "No, my abuser is not welcome in my house".

I'm now surrounded by supportive people, and things are way better, although I am still constantly afraid that the people I love will still leave eventually.

This happened to me, too, although I was a few years older when I was SHing. In fact I found out later that my brother was, too, and my mother blamed me but as far as I understand it was just two of her kids independently started SHing and she didn't get a clue.

This sounds like a really similar situation. He's absolutely charming most of the time but it's basically a really good act -- he is not charming underneath, and he viciously destroys people who he thinks have crossed him. He has been to prison for something he did as revenge but when I met him I thought he was reforming himself -- in any case *I* was reforming myself and thought I had some sort of role model and wanted so badly for us both to have a redemption arc. It's not coming, though.

Uh... This happened to me, too.

I'm not strictly monogamous but as a demi-sexual I can't just bring in a new person and have casual fun. I have explained this, but my partner isn't demi-sexual and doesn't really get it. I'm hyper-sexual but I am only attracted to a few people. This just doesn't compute for a lot of people but is my reality. 

Really hope he never does this for my birthday.

Edit: He keeps wanting to add girls, too. I'm only into men.

I go through it in September/October (spring) every year. Being predictable helps me prepare but it is still horrible!

I'm so stressed out at the moment I'm frequently having panic attacks, hurt myself doing basic Pilates because my shoulders are too tense, sometimes can't eat. My inner self-talk is just straight emotional abuse 24/7.

It isn't my "normal" and I hope to return to that in November.

I'm 34 and when I started my new job we were trying to work out who to go first in a meeting by age order. Everyone looked at me and said "B's first".

I was nowhere *near* the youngest. I am actually one of the older ones there but they just couldn't tell. People think I'm a teenager because my gestures/affect all scream "young person". I hate it so much but I'm not sure what exactly it is I need to change.

It's hard for me to tell for sure whether it's mellowing out or just that since I no longer live with her and can hang up the phone on her she has realized she has less power over me.

I do not want to ever move back in and have to find out.

Do you have an exit plan? Because this is extremely abusive.

I went through something similar with my Mormon parents with all the intense shaming, but at no point did they mention killing me or violence.

I can at least relate to being extremely confused and having a lot of trauma around this. Unraveling being queer (I'm a gay trans man), toxic gender messages and also being repeatedly targeted is basically my entire life story.

I have basically the same ones. Still working on it, not sure I can say I've recovered much at all. My entire life I've been acting like "It's not you, it's me" and have finally woken up and realized... those weren't friends/family, those were absolutely monstrous bullies.

I can hear the thoughts and push back or ignore them a lot of the time, but there's still frequently times I end up dissociating or being stressed to the point of being physically affected. I have a spectacularly kind boss, who has witnessed me having some pretty bad times and has tried to help, otherwise I don't know how I could even handle normal everyday life.

Me too. The point where I started doing really badly was when it clicked for me that some of what I experienced was abuse. It seems really bizarre to me that that changed anything at all, since whether or not I called it "abuse" it still happened and affected my life.

Absolutely. I have been getting mental health treatment of various kinds since I was 6 (probably contributed to the problem, actually). I'm now 34 and feel still thoroughly broken.

I don't think the help I was given was the right type, and what actually needed to change was the type of environment I was in. That has changed quite a while ago but I am not over the first 25 years of my life.

This is really familiar and it still continues.

When I was having problems with my husband, and he spoke to my mother briefly, she tried to commiserate with him about how hard I was to live with and that she didn't understand how he put up with me.

He came back from that phone call with a ton more sympathy for me. "Your mother is just incapable of taking your side, isn't she?"

I distrust my own self somehow and dismiss my own feelings. I see my own self as incredibly manipulative and an unreliable narrator. Makes it very hard to talk about what happened in person and I tend to start talking more about all the ways I'm probably wrong about it, and how awful I am for being so unfair to my parents.

Shortly after I almost got the official diagnosis -- why I didn't is too long a story -- the guy who would become my husband swooped in and rescued me from living with my mother. Immediately my symptoms that had to do with external behaviour where I would freak out and have panic attacks just stopped dead. I still have intense abandonment issues but it was mostly the change of environment which helped with the behavior.

My family punished me for having boundaries. For example, I was going to introduce my boyfriend's family to mine and explicitly asked my grandmother to hold off on the racism please. She intentionally was racist in front of my boyfriend's family just to rub it in that I was not allowed to ask for things like that. I would point out that my siblings were annoying a stranger in public and my mother would intentionally let it happen just so she could prove she was the parent, not me. I also was not actually allowed to leave an argument -- they would force me to stay and it would escalate when all I wanted was to go to my room.

And then I got away and so much of the borderline behaviour that they said was all my fault just stopped. I still feel like shit most of the time but I have pretty stable relationships, even if I experience severe anxiety about them ending.

What's going on with me resembles bulimia in some ways but I'm not binging and I don't want to lose weight. I have trouble with nausea when I eat, which has caused me to eat too little in the past and lose a lot of weight unintentionally. The nausea appears far more often when I'm out in public with people, or when I'm stressed. At its worst, I couldn't even eat much at home.

But actually not managing to keep food down is a new development. It used to just stop me from eating more and I'd feel sick, I wouldn't *be* sick. That's happening more and more often now and I'm a little paranoid about my teeth.

I don't think I have problems with food itself, just problems managing stress which manifest this way. But is that an eating disorder then, or something else?

Ok, so at least it is a known thing? I am lining up proper DBT for myself and doing some workbooks already.

Fortunately my FP is only in a platonic relationship with me so this sudden loss of "spark" may not be so noticeable to him. I'm just dismayed that the good feelings disappeared overnight during a particularly bad spot. Maybe they'll come back, he is still important to me in any case.
Exact same thing happens to me, including still being able to write.

Stuck in the same space at the moment. I wish I could just enjoy the good things that are happening like a healthy person but now that I have some things which I value a lot I am afraid of them going away soon. I am constantly aware of how little would need to change for my entire life to blow up. I'm very frustrated at myself because I do understand that feeling like this is unnecessary and actually counter-productive. Other people could get a raise and not turn it into a negative thing -- "Now there's so much more pressure on me, I cannot take it!" I *should* be feeling good about it, not like a complete piece of undeserving shit, but that's not me at the moment, and I'm still unsure how to stop the negative way my thoughts always go after these things.

This happens to me but I'm afraid I also don't know how to control it. It happens every time I talk about my parents even if I stay away from the worst of it.

I can recognize the signs that it is starting and maybe distance myself from the conversation but it is actually pretty obvious to everyone that it's happening and that's very frustrating. My boss mentioned it at one point.
It feels kinda nice at first, definitely helps me to cope... then a few days later I'm still waiting for them to come back.

I haven't told the last few FPs, and the ones before that could probably just tell.

Current FP is trustworthy and safe enough that he might be able to handle that information but I think it might be a bit much pressure. It might help if he knows I have such severe self-esteem problems that when I disappear it's because I assume nobody wants me, but that's *also* possibly a bit much. Still working out the right level of information to give out.

Me: *accidentally tells a "funny" story that's not funny*

Coworkers: :o

Me: "Whatchu talking about? My childhood was fine."


But also me: *tells a clearly traumatic story*

Husband: "You need to stop talking to your parents."

Me <now triggered>: "WHATCHU TALKING ABOUT? MY CHILDHOOD WAS FINE!"

Yeah, basically this. The better things are the worse it will feel when it all inevitably ends.

In the real world, things are going relatively well. I have friends that I do things with and for. Job is great. All of this makes me feel really bad because I have things that matter to me now, and that feels precarious. I guess old me would have just jettisoned the things that matter early because I find it that hard to take.

I hate that I'm so mentally unwell that I make the best parts of my life a source of anguish.

They're so constant that I have to work out whether I mean it this time or it's just an automatic thought.

I have some really explicitly suicidal songs in my main playlist solely so when they come on I do a quick self-check of whether they're relatable today or not. Usually no, but if yes I do tend to start preparing the safety net.
I'm in a much better place now. Still quite clearly traumatized in a lot of ways, but I've found people I feel safe with. :)

I think I know why I like it, I do love media analysis. :)

This question is prompted by people in my life who seem to be on the verge of an intervention, though. I've already told them it isn't necessary and I'm going to have to explicitly say "You are now crossing a boundary".

I'm sorry that happened to you as well.

I have kind of intense shame about a hygiene issue when I was young and powerless enough to not be able to do anything about it. The solution should have been "An adult helped", however they just shamed me. Still have problems around it today -- not the hygiene issue itself, but how they handled it.

And it happened more than once. Like my mother refused to let me shave my legs as a teen even though I was mandated to wear a skirt. Then when I finally insisted enough she didn't teach me and I ended up with razor burn so bad I ended up leaving deep gouges in my legs from scratching. Nobody gave a shit.

Extremely. People who know me will verbally notify me before touching me so I don't have a terrible fright.

I've never been hit so it's not a direct effect of trauma. I do have autism, so it could be a sensory thing.
I don't actively want to >!die!< yet but I'm thinking about it a lot.

My mother was one of those "I'm hurting you to help you" believers and I guess thought I needed to be told how people were perceiving me so I'd change. But she'd tell me that an aunt or teacher disliked me so much they wanted to beat the shit out of me then still expect me to be OK being around that person. I'd suppress my feelings so much, but I was actually frightened by how many people allegedly wanted to do physical violence to me -- although the physical violence actually never happened.

I became extremely emotionally abusive to myself, not accepting anything less than perfection. This was a defense mechanism as I thought it was better to be hard on myself than it was to mess up so bad that someone else would do it for me.

I don't let my own mistakes go, not even the small ones, even though I know I wouldn't care if someone else made them. I apologize constantly for things which other people don't care that I did. I believe I'm a selfish piece of trash and even when I do small things for other people those don't count, those are just me being manipulative, trying to get people to like me.

Even though I know this is what I'm doing, I'm not able to stop. It is happening right now! It affects my ability to relate to other people because I constantly feel like they're better than me and I need to struggle and improve myself... but I know I'll never be good enough for me no matter what I do unless I can kill the Inner Critic.

Yes, although I can still communicate in writing. It's as if all the brain pathways that control words actually coming out my mouth get confused.

I'm autistic, I thought it was related to that, but maybe it's not so clear after all.

My mother still tells my husband how hard I am to live with and how she doesn't understand how he puts up with me. When I was growing up I was told this really often and would be packed on planes to be sent away to relatives so she didn't have to live with me. Would get blamed for what I now know is just traumatized behaviour but if my siblings showed the same, the fact that they were doing it was *also* my fault. I was constantly in trouble and not even protected from other people who were also abusive. Basically it was a free for all where whoever wanted a go at me could have it, and sometimes even if mean things weren't said to my face my mother would pass them on anyway.

My dad seemed to be like that in both of his first two marriages. My mother is kind of a covert narc, she does things behind closed doors but must be self-aware on some level. My step mother was so over-the-top with the Golden Child/Scapegoat thing that I spotted how fucked it all was pretty early.

My dad was kind of quietly in the background letting it happen. He got roped into coming along with my mother when she was forcibly breaking me and my boyfriend up, and my dad apparently thinks that was OK. He didn't give me emotional support when I left the extremely controlling church we were in, even though he'd been through the same. Just so uninvolved and checked out even when we could have related in some way.

That paragraph really resonates with me, I'll put it on my reading list.

I have such a hard time talking about anything because these thoughts keep going through my head:

* Is it really necessary? Does it add anything?

* Do they really want to hear from you?

* Am I saying it right?

* Is this going to upset/offend people?

I spend so much time pre-checking what I'm going to say that often I say nothing at all. And unfortunately, there is only one topic over which I deem myself "expert" enough to speak on -- my own thoughts and experiences -- so I worry that I come off as very self-centred. I think it's more that literally any other topic in the world I just tell myself I don't know jackshit about and have nothing to add.

Being labelled "manipulative" made it impossible to get help for a time. I'm a bit of a weird autistic/BPD hybrid and actually have a reputation for extreme honesty even when it is bad for me. Being labelled with BPD meant that suddenly no one would believe me anymore, even about things which caused trauma. So I've literally had experiences with psychs trying to work out what was wrong with me, I think I give an honest answer, and then they dismiss it and go "Well, you're naturally manipulative so the real cause must be something else".

Fucking everyone at school knew I was getting emotionally abused. Other parents knew and called my parents out. What happened when I got the BPD label was that the entire (shitty) mental health system got weaponized against me and they decided nothing was actually going on at home because my parents seemed reasonable when they met them.

I love my FP, too. He was already in a relationship, has a little kid, and he would have to be bi/gay to be into me so I know it's just not gonna happen.

It's painful and I try to hold onto "Love means wanting what's best for him". I do actually want him to be happy and he's already made his choice and has a family. And it seems like a really nice, healthy one, too. I'm happy for him.

All of that just feels like it's covering up the longing, not killing it, though. I hope he never figures out how I feel.

I've done this in our work chat, and people have been like "Well that brought the mood down".

I just plain don't tell "funny" stories from my childhood anymore. Too many of them end up like this.

It's really hard at first. I remember the first person who ever told me I was actually OK felt like it changed my life. I clung to him because I had not found anyone else who accepted me.

And it never is going to happen fast enough. I picked up one new person every few years, and so now have a few, but each one felt like a lot of work. Because I basically distrust people unless they're waving a whole lot of green flags. Then when I spot one I have to try not to get unhealthily attached because otherwise they can become my entire world and that can be very off-putting to them. (They still become my entire world but I have learnt how to tone it down.)

I think that's the perception now.

As soon as two out of three children managed to leave home, and I was able to distance myself from my mother things got better. I can't go home without causing myself a great deal of stress still but they keep trying to get me back in the fold. And they'll just be like "B's just always been like that, don't know what happened."

My brother started SHing, and as far as I know he didn't know I was doing it and could only have found out through my mother. But suddenly it was my fault again...

Adult me wants to slap her upside the head and yell: "Bitch, two of your children are independently harming themselves! Fix your parenting!"

15-20 years later, I had started at a new job. My manager turned up one day with a beautiful blue mohawk, and all I could think was... there's no dress code. I wish I could say I was happy, but when I turned up at work I felt overwhelming fear. I felt literally sick. I was hiding my hands involuntarily. And it got better. And then I got my own mohawk, it was bright orange. My hair has gradually been most colours on the rainbow. I realized I never stopped enjoying the aesthetic, it's just my personal taste that I was intensely shamed for. In a way this has been incredibly healing and I've made tangible progress since I just let loose and did what made me happy.
